newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE WHEAT RISES AS FUTURES SEE TIGHT MARKET LOOMS.
newsitem.headline: SFE WHEAT RISES AS FUTURES SEE TIGHT MARKET LOOMS.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rose on Tuesday, reversing the trend of previous trading days, as prices gyrated on the prospect of essentially tight supply.
Turnover remained moderately heavy with 49 contracts changing hands, as buying interest spread into contracts which do not usually trade.

Nearby September 1997 traded A$5.00 a tonne higher to A$205.00, market leader January 1998 added A$1.00 to A$190.00, March 1998 rose A$2.50 to A$192.00 while the normally dormant May 1998 edged up by 50 cents to A$192.50 a tonne.
Settlement prices were variable but mostly up by about A$4.00. Four January 1998 put options traded at a A$170.00 strike price while three traded at a A$185.00 strike.
Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures attributed the market rise mainly to the certainty that wheat would be hotly contested on Australia's east coast, regardless of the 1997/98 crop size.
A market fall toward A$185.00 would trigger increased buying, with merchants realising they would need grain to keep business flowing, he said.
Additional factors were the USDA monthly crop report and the latest Australian Wheat Board wheat tender sale, he said.
